Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-29
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Elden), Omar Khalid (Elden DevOps), Priya Shah (Product), Samir Patel (Data Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (auto - may be imperfect):
Quick weekly sync to review POC quality metrics; triage a spike in hallucination-style false positives for the clinical triage prompt set; agree next steps for regression sweep, security validation and pricing for a potential pilot extension. Talked about Dedicated vs Private considerations for data residency; briefly touched on SSO and KMS.

Topics: Scorecard drift, guardrail tuning, prompt pruning, regression sweep plan, SSO/KMS validation, pilot extension pricing

Transcript body:
00:00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we have about 50 minutes, is that still good?
00:00:05 Dr. Lena Ortiz: yes yep that's fine um quick note we have Priya and Samir joining from product and data engineering.
00:00:12 Maya Chen: perfect great. quick one - Diego from our side will walk the latest scorecard, then we'll triage the regression spike on the clinical triage prompts.
00:00:20 Diego Ramos: cool hi all, so I'll share my screen — one sec, i'm, uh, getting the spreadsheet.
00:00:35 Diego Ramos: ok so this is the week-over-week scorecard. overall pass rate is stable at 87%, but the clinical_triage_v2 prompt set shows a drop to 72% on precision for red-flag detection, that's where the false positives have jumped.
00:00:52 Priya Shah: can you define the red-flag detection metric again? like is that precision or recall?
00:00:58 Diego Ramos: good question — for that signal we evaluate both, but the scorecard column called "red_flag_precision" is how often the model labeled a normal case as red-flag incorrectly, so higher is worse. we want precision high (like 95% target), but it's down.
00:01:15 Samir Patel: just to add, the dataset for that prompt set grew by about 12% this sprint because product added new edge cases from recent logs. maybe distribution shift.
00:01:25 Dr. Lena Ortiz: yeah we saw more examples where the language is ambiguous, like negations and longitudinal phrasing — model seems to over-trigger.
00:01:33 Diego Ramos: possibilities — prompt drift, new data patterns, or we pushed a slightly different model variant during the weekend (small quantization tweak).
00:01:42 Maya Chen: hmm can you expand on the quantization tweak? was that our dedicated infra config or a hosted model change?
00:01:50 Diego Ramos: it's a config change we recommended to save tokens for the pilot — a 4-bit quant baseline on the smaller Llama-based variant. it shouldn't effect classification usually but at the margin it can shift confidence calibration.
00:02:05 Omar Khalid: quick ops question — were those requests routed to Dedicated pools or the hosted api? network logs show some requests hitting both.
00:02:15 Diego Ramos: good catch — we had routing policy change last Friday to prefer Dedicated for your tenant but fallback to hosted if capacity exceeded. there were short windows where fallbacks occurred.
00:02:26 Priya Shah: so fallback may have introduced a different model binary? could that explain the spikes?
00:02:33 Diego Ramos: possibly yes — different model variant and quant profile on hosted vs dedicated. Also there is caching behavior that can change prefix handling.
00:02:40 Dr. Lena Ortiz: ok so root cause could be mixture of routing and data drift. what's the plan to triage?
00:02:47 Diego Ramos: suggested steps — 1) run regression sweep only on clinical_triage_v2 with both variants (dedicated vs hosted) and both quant profiles; 2) sample false positives and label for root cause (prompt vs model); 3) try prompt surgery options (add explicit negative examples, reduce temperature, add guardrail explicit check).
00:03:05 Maya Chen: agreed we'll run a 48-hour sweep. Diego can you pick the sample size?
00:03:11 Diego Ramos: i'll do 5k random + the top 200 near-threshold cases.
00:03:16 Priya Shah: for acceptance criteria when do we decide to rollback vs tune?
00:03:22 Maya Chen: good ops question — Priya, we recommended a rollback if precision drops below 80% for red-flag AND customer perception impact (e.g., more than 10% of tickets fired). But final decision with you.
00:03:34 Priya Shah: okay let's keep that threshold but we might tighten later.
00:03:38 Dr. Lena Ortiz: can we also confirm which guardrail rules are applied — are you using synthetic rule-based checks before model output?
00:03:46 Diego Ramos: yes there's a prefix guardrail layer and an output post-filter. however some of your cases are borderline and the model's outputs escape simple regex-style filters. We can add more deterministic checks in the pipeline though.
00:04:00 Samir Patel: what about using calibrated confidence scores and a fallback to human triage? that would reduce false positives at the cost of throughput.
00:04:08 Maya Chen: that's a common tradeoff — we can route low-confidence red-flag calls to human queue. You can tune that threshold in Console per route.
00:04:16 Dr. Lena Ortiz: is confidence reliable after quantization?
00:04:21 Diego Ramos: it's slightly less calibrated, we recommend temperature=0.0 for classification prompts and then recalibrate with Platt scaling on a held-out subset. quantization affects logits shape minimally but calibration needs to be re-learned.
00:04:35 Omar Khalid: another ops item — we need to test SSO provisioning. we tried SAML test and it failed for one user (error: assertion consumer mismatch).
00:04:44 Maya Chen: we have a SAML SSO checklist, i'll share. sometimes ACS URL formatting differs between IdPs.
00:04:51 Omar Khalid: also KMS — we want to ensure customer-managed keys are used on Private deployment. any blockers?
00:05:00 Diego Ramos: Private supports KMS/HSM integration; for Dedicated we offer encryption at rest with our managed keys by default and optional BYOK in enterprise tier. For the pilot, we can enable customer KMS if you move to Private or dedicated enterprise.
00:05:14 Priya Shah: cost implications?
00:05:17 Maya Chen: BYOK and Private have an administrative fee and some setup time, we'll share details in the doc.
00:05:23 Dr. Lena Ortiz: back to the regression - Diego, can you show a couple of sample failure cases?
00:05:28 Diego Ramos: yep — sample 1: input mentions "patient denies chest pain, reported dizziness" and model marked as 'urgent' due to dizziness being over-weighted.
00:05:40 Samir Patel: that's tricky, the data often writes negations oddly.
00:05:44 Diego Ramos: Sample 2: long history notes where the model echoed an old red-flag phrase; the guardrail didn't detect because it was partially paraphrased.
00:05:54 Priya Shah: would canonicalizing language at preprocessing help? like run a clinical NLP normalizer?
00:06:01 Samir Patel: we have a light normalizer in preprocessing but it's not capturing tense/negation specifics; we can extend it but that adds pipeline complexity.
00:06:10 Maya Chen: tradeoff again — more preprocessing reduces model ambiguity but increases engineering overhead. Maybe do a short list of high-impact normalizations first.
00:06:18 Dr. Lena Ortiz: also we should check evaluation metrics; some of our labelers were inconsistent last sprint. labeling noise could look like model regression.
00:06:27 Priya Shah: agree, we had two labelers with different guidelines. Samir can you audit a 200-sample set?
00:06:32 Samir Patel: yes I'll audit and produce an inter-annotator agreement measure.
00:06:36 Diego Ramos: good — parallel actions: i'll run variant sweep, samir audits labels, maya and priya align on acceptance thresholds.
00:06:44 Maya Chen: timeline? Diego 48 hours, Samir by EOD next Monday?
00:06:49 Samir Patel: yes I can do EOD Monday.
00:06:52 Priya Shah: fine.
00:06:53 Dr. Lena Ortiz: also i'd like a mini-playbook - if the dedicated variant is better but Dedicated isn't available at scale, what's the plan?
00:07:02 Diego Ramos: fallback policy options — we can pin routing to Dedicated for critical endpoints; or use model variant parity across hosted and dedicated (deploy same quant profile). There's also traffic-splitting with canary thresholds.
00:07:13 Maya Chen: and we can apply automatic fallback to human triage for low confidence only for the clinical route.
00:07:19 Omar Khalid: firewall/peering note — if we evaluate Private you'll need a short window to set up VPC peering; can you send the network checklist?
00:07:26 Maya Chen: yes network checklist and a minimal firewall rule set, sending after the call.
00:07:31 Diego Ramos: quick technical aside — we noticed one regression correlated with longer context lengths; when transcripts hit >1,600 tokens the model latency also increases and some KV cache alignment is different which can change output.
00:07:43 Priya Shah: oh interesting, maybe some older notes are being included. can we add a prompt template to truncate or summarize history?
00:07:50 Diego Ramos: yes Redwood Console has a history summarization knob; we can also auto-prune by relevance. We'll propose a conservative 800-token history window for clinical triage.
00:08:01 Dr. Lena Ortiz: that's ok, but ensure summaries do not remove critical chronology.
00:08:06 Maya Chen: noted.
00:08:10 Priya Shah: any update on pricing for extension? we might need extra runway for the regression work.
00:08:15 Maya Chen: I have a pilot extension worksheet — short answer, we can extend 30 days at the same committed rate with an incremental fee for dedicated reserved slots. i'll send the breakdown.
00:08:26 Priya Shah: we'll review.
00:08:29 Diego Ramos: quick note on evaluation — we discovered a small bug in the scorecard script that incorrectly aggregated micro vs macro averages. fixed in the latest commit so some numbers changed slightly.
00:08:41 Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks — please post the commit hash.
00:08:44 Diego Ramos: sure will do.
00:08:47 Maya Chen: ok moving to guardrails — are you comfortable with current post-filters or do you want a policy layer?
00:08:55 Dr. Lena Ortiz: we want a clearer policy layer — e.g., explicit allow/deny decisions stored in an audit log for compliance.
00:09:03 Diego Ramos: Redwood Console can output audit logs per request; with Private or Dedicated enterprise tier we can push logs to your SIEM. Should also mention retention options.
00:09:13 Omar Khalid: retention needs to be configurable to 90 days to match org policy.
00:09:18 Maya Chen: noted — we'll include retention options in the security doc.
00:09:22 Priya Shah: Are there performance regressions we should worry about if we enable extra guardrails?
00:09:27 Diego Ramos: light rule checks are negligible; heavy deterministic checks or external calls add latency. If you need low 100s ms SLOs we recommend moving heavier logic to async or batched human queues.
00:09:40 Dr. Lena Ortiz: can we do a targeted AB test for the guardrail?
00:09:44 Maya Chen: yes, Console supports A/B routing and canary rollout for guardrail changes.
00:09:49 Priya Shah: ok that sounds good.
00:09:52 Diego Ramos: turning to concrete next steps — i'll run the regression across both variants and quant profiles and share a spreadsheet with sample cases, labeled reasons (prompt, model, data), and suggested mitigations.
00:10:04 Samir Patel: i'll audit labeler consistency and provide a corrected sample set.
00:10:09 Maya Chen: I'll share SSO docs, Private/KMS checklist, and the pilot extension pricing.
00:10:15 Priya Shah: i'll finalize success metrics and send top-20 prompts we want to lock for day-one.
00:10:21 Dr. Lena Ortiz: on decision rules: if regression is model-variant caused and dedicated variant improves >10% precision, we will request pinning to dedicated and discuss capacity.
00:10:32 Maya Chen: understood, we'll prepare capacity options and cost delta.
00:10:37 Diego Ramos: any other blockers?
00:10:39 Priya Shah: nothing from product.
00:10:41 Omar Khalid: ops only wants the network checklist and a weekend maintenance window option.
00:10:46 Maya Chen: will do.
00:10:50 Dr. Lena Ortiz: timeline recap — Diego 48h sweep, Samir audit by Monday EOD, Priya finalize acceptance 2027-01-04, Maya send docs by 2027-01-05.
00:10:59 Maya Chen: yes and we'll meet next Thursday same time for a quick readout — does that work?
00:11:05 Priya Shah: yes works.
00:11:07 Dr. Lena Ortiz: good thanks everyone.
00:11:11 Maya Chen: quick call wrap — I'll send the spreadsheet template and the playbook snippet you asked for.
00:11:18 Diego Ramos: and i'll attach a handful of representative cases in the sheet.
00:11:22 Omar Khalid: thanks all.
00:11:24 Maya Chen: ok thanks, we'll follow up in email. bye.
